name: South Ridge / McAllister Glacier
approach: Trailhead is the Eldorado Creek climbers' trailhead on Cascade River Road, roughly mile 20 out of Marblemount, at about 2,100 ft. From the parking pullout, backtrack a short distance downstream along the road to find a log or braided crossing of the Cascade River; ford/cross and pick up the unsigned but well-trodden climbers' path on the far bank, angling up through heavy timber. This boot path is steep and root-laced, gaining roughly 1,800-1,900 ft through forest before breaking out at a boulder field around 4,000 ft; follow cairns and the intermittent trail on the right side of the talus (roughly 1,000 vertical ft of boulder-hopping) up into the open meadows of Eldorado Creek/Eldorado Basin. From the basin, continue up benches toward the toe of the Eldorado Glacier (often called Eldorado Camp, ~6,000-7,500 ft) - this is a reasonable first-night camp and the last reliable running water before the ice cap. Rope up here: the Eldorado Glacier is broken and thinly bridged in a normal-to-low snow year, and parties have needed to weave crevasse mazes even on the standard line. From upper Eldorado Glacier, traverse north below Eldorado's east ridge and continue on the Inspiration Glacier toward Klawatti Col (~7,800 ft) - this leg is long, exposed to whiteout (several parties describe navigating the Inspiration's crevasse fields with zero visibility), and is the standard second camp for the Eldorado Ice Cap traverse that accesses Primus. From Klawatti Col camp, the climb of Primus itself is a summit-day push: down-climb or make a short (~50 ft) rappel through the notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col onto the Klawatti Glacier. Rope up, traverse north and then east below the south side of Austera's east ridge, descending to round the end of that ridge near 6,800 ft onto the North Klawatti Glacier, and cross it (probing for hidden crevasses - this section has caught parties by surprise even in good visibility) to the foot of Primus's south face. Unrope and climb snow ramps and then talus up the face, moving right onto the south ridge for the last couple of hundred feet to the 8,508 ft summit. The trailhead sits about 6,400 ft below the summit, and the round trip takes two to three days or more; mid-to-late summer (glacier bridges more consolidated, less whiteout risk) is the recommended window.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: Start at the Eldorado Creek climbers' trailhead at about mile 20 of Cascade River Road, east of Marblemount; cross the Cascade River on logs just downstream of the parking to reach the climbers' path.

approach_variants.name: The far end of the Eldorado ice cap: five glaciers and a notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col
approach_variants.notes:
This is the way to Primus's south side, and it comes from the opposite side of the mountain to the Thunder Creek approach. From the Eldorado Creek trailhead on Cascade River Road near 2,100 ft, cross the Cascade River, climb the steep root-laced boot path through timber, cross the boulder field around 4,000 ft following cairns on the right side of the talus, and reach the meadows of Eldorado Basin. Continue to the toe of the Eldorado Glacier and rope up — it is broken and thinly bridged in a normal-to-low snow year.

From the upper Eldorado Glacier, traverse north below Eldorado's east ridge and continue on the Inspiration Glacier toward Klawatti Col near 7,800 ft. Parties describe crossing the Inspiration's crevasse fields with zero visibility, so plan for it.

Summit day from a Klawatti Col camp: downclimb or make a short rappel of about 50 ft through the notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col onto the Klawatti Glacier, rope up, and traverse below the south side of Austera's east ridge, rounding its end near 6,800 ft onto the North Klawatti Glacier — probing, because this stretch has caught parties by surprise even in good visibility — to the foot of Primus's south side. Then unrope and walk.

The route crosses the Eldorado, Inspiration, McAllister, Klawatti and North Klawatti glaciers in sequence; Austera Towers is passed and bypassed on a short scree ramp along the glacier's eastern edge.
approach_variants.season: Mid-July through August, when the glacier bridges are most consolidated and whiteout risk is lowest
hazards: A heavily crevassed North Klawatti and McAllister glacier system, especially late season
Thin, unreliable snow bridges by August and September — probe before committing weight
Complex glacier route-finding around Klawatti Col in poor visibility
A short technical step at the McAllister-Klawatti notch that has to be reversed at the end of the day
Extreme remoteness: a multi-day approach with no cell coverage
approach_variants.baseFinding: The one findable feature on this route is the notch at the McALLISTER-Klawatti Col, and it is findable because it is the only place all day you need a rope for rock. It is a step of roughly 50 ft: downclimbed, hand-lined, or rappelled off a sling on a horn or block — there is no fixed hardware. If you have crossed a col without a technical step, you are not through it yet. After the notch, the test is what you are standing on rather than what you can see. You drop onto the Klawatti Glacier, traverse below Austera's east ridge and round its end onto the North Klawatti Glacier. The climbing begins where you take the rope off: snow-covered talus, class 2-3, straight to the 8,508 ft summit. There is no notch, no rib and no marked start above the glacier — the honest answer is that this route has no rock landmark at its base, and the col behind you is what tells you where you are. The negative test is the strong one and it settles the whole peak: the other standard line on Primus is reached from Thunder Creek, and it starts at Lucky Pass — a notch at the head of the Borealis Glacier where the route to Tricouni Peak splits off east. If you are at a pass with a second peak's route leaving it, you are on the east slope and you came up the wrong valley for this route. The two lines are on opposite sides of the mountain and share no ground below the summit. And watch the false summit whatever side you came from: a false top stands around 8,270 ft and is passed on climber's-left. A high point reached without traversing round anything is not the summit.

approach_variants.name: Thunder Creek and the Borealis Glacier: the east ridge from Lucky Pass
approach_variants.notes:
The other way onto Primus comes from the north, and it finishes on a different line: the east ridge, not this route's south side. From Colonial Creek Campground on the North Cascades Highway, walk the Thunder Creek Trail about six miles to McAllister Camp. The bridge over Thunder Creek there has washed out, so expect to ford cold, fast water or hunt for a log crossing.

Across the creek, a faint, steep boot path climbs the long, brushy lower north ridge of Tricouni Peak to the toe of the Borealis Glacier near 6,000 ft, where there is good camping. From camp, climb the glacier along its eastern edge, keeping clear of the icefall in its middle, to Lucky Pass, the col between Primus and Tricouni near 7,200 ft, and follow the east ridge to the summit on class 3 ground.

The brush on the ridge above Thunder Creek is slow going in either direction, and worse carrying skis or a long pack.
hazards: An unbridged ford of Thunder Creek at McAllister Camp
A steep, brushy boot path that is easy to lose on the ridge above Thunder Creek
An icefall in the middle of the Borealis Glacier that has to be skirted
Class 3 ground on the east ridge above Lucky Pass

waypoints.name: Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.note: Climbers' parking at about mile 20 of Cascade River Road, near 2,100 ft. The unsigned path starts by crossing the Cascade River on logs a short way downstream of the parking.
waypoints.directions: From SR-20 in Marblemount, cross the Skagit River onto the Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles, gravel after about mile 10, to the Eldorado climbers' parking near milepost 20 at about 2,100 ft. Overnight camps need a backcountry permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

waypoints.name: Primus Peak
waypoints.note: Reached from a camp at Klawatti Col across the Klawatti and North Klawatti glaciers, then snow ramps and talus up the south face to the upper south ridge; glacier travel gear required.
waypoints.directions: Cross the river on a log just downstream of the parking and climb the steep climbers' path and the boulder field near 4,000 ft into Eldorado Basin. Rope up and cross the Eldorado and Inspiration Glaciers north to Klawatti Col, pass the 50 ft notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col onto the Klawatti Glacier, round Austera's east ridge onto the North Klawatti Glacier, and scramble talus up the south face to the summit.

descent_text: Descend by reversing the ascent line: down-climb the summit talus back to the North Klawatti Glacier, rope back up, and re-cross the glacier (same crevasse-probing caution as the approach) to the base of the McAllister-Klawatti notch. Regaining the notch back up to Klawatti Col camp is normally a climb/scramble rather than a rappel; the technical crux of the day - the short ~50 ft step between the notch and the glacier - is the one spot parties commonly fix a hand line or short rappel on the way down from the ridge, then climb the same step (with a boost from a partner or a fixed line) on the return leg. Primus's west-ridge line has a similar ~8,200 ft notch requiring a roughly 50 ft rappel to regain the glacier when descending, which lines up with an account of a party rappelling at the McAllister-Klawatti col - treat this as a single, short technical rappel rather than a multi-pitch rap descent. A single 30-60m rope is more than sufficient (a doubled 30m or single 60m easily covers 50-60 ft); anchors are natural (slings on horns/blocks) rather than bolted, since this is remote glaciated terrain with no fixed hardware. From Klawatti Col camp, the multi-day exit reverses the approach: back across the Inspiration Glacier (whiteout and crevasse hazard again), down the Eldorado Glacier, through Eldorado Basin, down the boulder field and timber climbers' path, and back across the Cascade River to the trailhead. Watch for softening glacier bridges and increased rockfall/scree looseness on the boulder-field descent in the afternoon heat.

pitch_detail.notes: From the Eldorado Creek trailhead (~2,100 ft), cross the Cascade River and climb the steep path through timber and the boulder field near 4,000 ft into Eldorado Basin and on to the toe of the Eldorado Glacier.
Cross the Eldorado and Inspiration Glaciers, weaving through crevasses, to a camp near Klawatti Col (~7,800 ft).
Downclimb or make a short rappel through the notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col onto the Klawatti Glacier.
Traverse below the south side of Austera's east ridge, round its end near 6,800 ft onto the North Klawatti Glacier, and cross it, probing for hidden cracks, to the foot of Primus's south face.
Unrope and scramble snow-covered talus, passing a false summit near 8,270 ft on climber's left, to the 8,508 ft summit.
